title.narrative: OEGI- Ground Water Exploration and Assessment

description.narrative: (Kenya): The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) supports the Government of Kenya with remote sensing, mapping, and groundwater modeling to determine the amount of ground water availability in Kenya. USGS will work with local partners to identify sources of existing hydrogeologic and hydrologic data; acquire and interpret remotely sensed data; generate preliminary maps for groundwater supply development; identify data gaps and develop plans for investigations; evaluate conceptual models to interpret remotely-sensed data; conduct training sessions on these findings. The activity will provide data on productive water aquifers suitable for human consumption, and contribute to long-term planning for drinking water. Kenya is classified as water scarce country with average freshwater supply estimated to be half of the UN's threshold for water scarcity. In water scarce areas, natural resource conflicts are increasing. The funds will expand the mapping of groundwater resources to additional counties, train government of Kenya staff on the application of data, and develop a platform for overall groundwater coordination efforts. The activity promotes sustainability by empowering county and national governments and their water companies to effectively manage their water resources. These efforts directly contribute to the US Global Water Strategy Strategic Objective Two: Encourage the sound management and protection of freshwater resources. This activity will help address water scarcity challenges, which can exacerbate political instability and cause social unrest, thus contributing to greater regional stability, a U.S. foreign policy objective. $100,000 of funding within this IM contributes to meeting the required "adaptation indirect" earmark". Studies include identification of recharge areas. This enables communities and host governments to ensure they are conserved to help replenish the groundwater which will help to reduce risks associated with climate change.
